mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across historical easing cycles without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions with unemployment below 4.0%, labor market overheating generates inflationary pressures that trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 95.0 (2017=100), it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) indicate inflationary monetary tightening, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: The joint condition CPIAUCSL>3.0 and FEDFUNDS>4.0 fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In housing market booms with housing starts above 1000.0 (thousands of units), strong consumer confidence drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated retail spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST > 1000.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate generates immediate accommodative policy signals that compress short-term equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
